data.text: When anyone presents a grain offering to the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour. He shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.
data.titulo: The Grain Offering and Its Memorial Portion

data.text: He shall bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. The priest shall take from it his full handful of its fine flour and oil, with all its frankincense, and turn its memorial portion into smoke on the altar, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
What is left of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy portion of the offerings by fire to the LORD.
When you present a grain offering baked in an oven, it shall be of fine flour: unleavened cakes mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it shall be of fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.
Break it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering prepared in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
You shall bring the grain offering made from these things to the LORD. The one bringing it shall present it to the priest, and the priest shall bring it near the altar.
The priest shall take its memorial portion from the grain offering and turn it into smoke on the altar, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
What is left of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy portion of the offerings by fire to the LORD.
No grain offering that you present to the LORD shall be made with leaven, for you shall not turn any leaven or any honey into smoke as an offering by fire to the LORD.
data.titulo: Leaven, Firstfruits, and the Salt of the Covenant

data.text: You may present them to the LORD as an offering of firstfruits, but they shall not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
You shall season every grain offering of yours with salt. You shall not let the salt of the covenant of your God be lacking from your grain offering. With all your offerings you shall present salt.
If you present a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, you shall present young heads of grain roasted in the fire, crushed fresh grain, as your grain offering of firstfruits.
You shall put oil on it and place frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.
The priest shall turn its memorial portion into smoke, some of its crushed grain and its oil with all its frankincense, an offering by fire to the LORD.
